correctness.rationale: Write r=√2−1. Octagonal dihedral symmetries reduce x to (1,t), 0<=t<=r, and sign of y to the upper semicircle. Each right/left vertical boundary forces one chord norm 2, each slanted boundary makes the Schäffer max strictly exceed √2 except a shared top endpoint, and on top y=(a,1) the inequalities N(x+y)<=√2 and N(x−y)<=√2 are exactly a+t<=0 and a+t>=0. Therefore necessarily a=−t, i.e. y=Qx (up to symmetry/sign), with both chord norms √2. All other pairs have max>√2. This proves C_S=√2 and iff minimizers, not merely finite sampling.

value.rationale: A complete equality-case classification for the natural Schäffer inf-max companion to James sup-min is a structural rigidity result: every minimizing pair is an exact Euclidean quarter turn and therefore also a James maximizer. This supplies pair-level geometry beyond the known scalar value, and the coincidence of the two extremizer sets is not implied by their numerical constant product.
